name: Rubin Legacy Survey of Space and Time Camera
description: The 3.2-gigapixel imaging camera installed on the Simonyi Survey Telescope at Cerro Pachón, Chile, was built for repeated wide-field imaging in the Legacy Survey of Space and Time.

places.note: DOE SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, where the camera was assembled.
Simonyi Survey Telescope on Cerro Pachón.

date.label: by 2024-04
date.basis: Camera complete by the April 2024 public announcement. Exact completion day unresolved.

events.statement: SLAC completed construction of the 3.2-gigapixel LSST Camera before its transport to Chile.

evidence.locator: Paragraphs on completed camera and optical system
evidence.supports: The operator dates completion and describes the camera that was later shipped and installed.

date.basis: The operator dates first on-sky engineering imagery to this day.

events.statement: Rubin's installed LSST Camera acquired its first on-sky engineering images.

evidence.locator: §3, On-sky commissioning began with LSST Camera
evidence.supports: Dates the first images with the installed LSST Camera and identifies the commissioning scope.

date.basis: Date of the public press event.

events.statement: Rubin publicly released First Look images from commissioning observations.
events.place_note: Release venue for imagery obtained at Cerro Pachón in Chile.

evidence.supports: Dates the public event and identifies the data as test imagery.

date.basis: Official start date given by the observatory's science page.

events.statement: Rubin began the formal Legacy Survey of Space and Time with its installed camera.

evidence.supports: The operator's science page dates actual survey start.

earliest_record.rationale: Dates the completed instrument. The first observations and formal survey use are distinct milestones.

caveats: The 144-megapixel Commissioning Camera was a separate test instrument used in 2024. The February 2026 alert stream preceded the formal survey.
